@@U04022@@
On my way here, I noticed our worthy Emperor has got himself into a mess. Well, you know what he’s like. That time we entertained him and inundated him in paper money, you'd have thought the whole world was up for grabs. He came quite young to the throne— scarcely a beard to his chin— and arrived at the false though rather convenient conclusion that pleasure and imperial power were harmonious bedfellows.

@@U04024@@
A grave mistake! A ruler must find his sole satisfaction in ruling. His heart must be filled with a high will and purpose, but no man should be able to divine its contents. Those secrets are alone for the ears of intimates; he has only to suggest, and it is done, and all the world stands amazed. In this way he will always reign supreme. Pleasure makes a man common.

@@U04026@@
He’s not like that. While he took his pleasure the empire collapsed into anarchy. Great and small were at each other’ throats, brother banished and murdered brother, castle warred with castle, town with town, guilds fought with gentry, bishops with chapter and parish. A wayward glance was enough to make an enemy. Your life wasn’t safe even in a church.
translation:
@@U04022@@
在我来这里的路上，我发现我们尊贵的皇帝已经陷入了困境。好吧，你知道他是什么样的。那次我们招待他，给他大量的纸币，你会以为整个世界都可供争夺。他很年轻就登上了王位——下巴上几乎没有胡子——并得出了一个错误但相当方便的结论：享乐和皇权是和谐共存的。

@@U04024@@
一个严重的错误！统治者必须在统治中找到唯一的满足。他的内心必须充满崇高的意志和目标，但没有人能够预测其内容。这些秘密只有亲密的人才能听到。他只需要提出建议，事情就完成了，全世界都惊讶不已。如此一来，他将永远占据至高无上的地位。快乐使人变得平凡。

@@U04026@@
他不是那样的。当他享乐时，帝国却陷入了无政府状态。大大小小互相争斗，兄弟放逐或谋杀兄弟，城堡与城堡交战，城镇与城镇交战，行会与贵族争斗，主教与教区和教区争斗。任性的一个眼神就足以树敌。即使在教堂里，你的生活也不安全。
